title: The Groove Line
year_note: GTO released the single in November 1977 ahead of the album Central Heating (UK 1977, US 1978). It entered the UK chart on 14 January 1978 and peaked on the Hot 100 in July 1978.

notes.made: Temperton wrote it for the second album, which Barry Blue produced across five London studios (Audio International, Utopia, Morgan, the Marquee and AIR) with James Guthrie and Geoff Calver engineering and John Cameron arranging. Keith Wilder sings lead over Johnnie's chorus, and the touring band played their own parts with very few session players. Temperton is on Rhodes, clavinet, synths and organ, and takes a jazzy piano solo in the middle.
notes.context: This was Heatwave's third American hit and their biggest pop one after "Boogie Nights": number seven on the Hot 100 and three on the soul chart in July 1978, as the Saturday Night Fever soundtrack was ending 24 weeks at number one. Britain had it first and took it to 12. Central Heating was the last album with Mantese and guitarist Eric Johns, and Temperton's last as a member, though he kept writing for the band until 1982.

listen_for.note: A chugging rhythm guitar, hand claps and horn blasts carry Keith Wilder's lead, with Johnnie's chorus answering him.
Temperton's own jazzy piano solo, the keyboard player stepping out on his own song.

leads_to.title: Mind Blowing Decisions
leads_to.why: Johnnie Wilder's own song from Central Heating, a smooth Philly-style soul tune that made 12 in the UK in June 1978 and shows the band had a second writer.

notes.unverified: Wikipedia says Public Enemy sampled it on "Sophisticated Bitch" (1987), but the claim carries a citation-needed tag, so it is left out. The Rock with You link comes from a SoulTracks article I could read only in search excerpts.

culture.title: Top ten in America
culture.line: Number seven on the Hot 100 and three on the soul chart in 1978; the RIAA certified it platinum in 2001.

culture.title: Blockster's "Grooveline"
culture.line: The British DJ Blockster's 1999 remake reached 18 on the UK Singles Chart and two on the UK dance chart.
